title: Ada and the Veil
premise: Silas Halloran, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-free city of Greyhollow, discovers his name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies. The prophecy binds him to Ada Vey, a memory-thief who unknowingly carries the stolen soul of the true heir to the court beneath the mountain—the soul Silas himself sold to save his sister twelve years ago. As the usurper's armies march on the free cities, Silas and Ada must infiltrate the subterranean court, where reclaiming the soul will erase every memory Ada has of their journey together and expose Silas's betrayal of her trust. In the end, Silas chooses truth over safety: he returns the soul and confesses everything, and Ada—stripped of her memories but not her instincts—chooses to walk beside him anyway, proving that loyalty can outlast memory itself.
about_author: Felix Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forbidden grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who lie well and love badly.

chapters.title: The Charm-Seller's Tuesday
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A quiet evening selling luck-knots in Greyhollow is shattered when a customer's purchase triggers a vision of storm-light. Silas realizes his wards are failing and someone is hunting magic in the city. Emotional beat: the fragile comfort of invisibility beginning to crack.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Dust
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada, a memory-thief who steals recollections for coin, breaks into the archive of a dead prophet and finds a prophecy naming 'the storm-caller' on this exact date—with her own face sketched beside it. Emotional beat: unease at being written about before she lived it.

chapters.title: Two Thieves, One Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ada confronts Silas at his stall; he denies being a storm-caller while lightning flickers under his skin. They strike a wary bargain to investigate the prophecy together. Emotional beat: mutual suspicion laced with reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: What the Prophet Buried
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Digging through the prophet's sealed cellar, Silas finds the full prophecy: the heir's soul will be returned by the one who sold it, or the usurper's armies will reach the free cities by winter. He recognizes his own crime. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing after twelve years of burial.

chapters.title: The Weight She Carries
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada examines her own memories for tampering and finds a locked vault inside her mind she never made—one humming with borrowed soul-light. She begins to suspect what she carries. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering your own head is not entirely yours.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Door
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The Ministry of Unmaking raids Greyhollow's market following rumors of live magic. Silas burns his charms and flees with Ada, abandoning the identity he built over twelve years. Emotional beat: grief for a small, safe life that was always a lie.

chapters.title: Road Beneath Rain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the road toward the mountain, Ada teaches Silas her memory-craft while he, guilt-ridden, deflects questions about his exile. First real laughter between them. Emotional beat: intimacy growing in the space honesty hasn't yet reached.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Waited
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A detour reveals his sister Wren alive but hollow-eyed, kept as leverage by the usurper's agents since the day he sold the soul. She begs him not to come for her. Emotional beat: the cost of his old bargain made flesh.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada secretly reads one of Silas's surface memories and glimpses the sale—a soul traded, a sister spared—and misreads whose soul it was. She says nothing. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against the hunger for truth.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Herald
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The armies burn a waystation ahead of schedule; a herald offers Silas amnesty if he delivers 'the vessel'—Ada—to the mountain. Silas refuses and kills the herald, crossing a line. Emotional beat: protective rage hardening into commitment.

chapters.title: City of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Sheltering in a refugee city, Ada meets others who carry stolen things and learns the vault in her mind is a prison-cell for a soul, not a storage-room. The heir inside dreams through her. Emotional beat: compassion for the stranger living behind her eyes.

chapters.title: Storm-Called Confession
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Cornered by Ada's direct question, Silas confesses partially: he sold a soul to the court beneath the mountain, but claims it was a stranger's. The lie lands like a stone between them. Emotional beat: shame choosing survival over truth.

chapters.title: The Gate of Teeth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the mountain's mouth, passing trials that strip travelers of disguises—including, nearly, Silas's human guise. Ada sees the storm-light fully for the first time. Emotional beat: awe and fear braided together.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Descending into the subterranean court, Silas faces the Broker who bought the soul and learns the price of return: the carrier loses all memories formed since receiving it. Every mile with Ada would vanish from her. Emotional beat: horror at a price paid in shared time.

chapters.title: The Heir Speaks Through Her
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The imprisoned heir surfaces in Ada's dreams, showing her the usurper's coup a century past—and showing her Silas kneeling in that memory, younger, making his terrible trade. She wakes knowing everything. Emotional beat: betrayal and understanding arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Lies
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ada confronts Silas; he finally tells the whole truth—Wren, the sale, the prophecy, the erasure awaiting her. She walks away into the court's gilded halls alone. Emotional beat: heartbreak as the consequence of long-deferred honesty.

chapters.title: The Broker's Bargain
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Alone, Silas negotiates with the Broker, offering his own storm-magic—his identity, his power—as collateral for the soul's release. The Broker accepts, delighted. Emotional beat: self-annihilation offered freely at last.

chapters.title: Usurper's Arrival
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The usurper's vanguard breaches the mountain to seize both soul and throne. Ada, memory intact for now, rallies the court's forgotten loyalists using the heir's dream-memories as proof. Emotional beat: courage kindled from another's borrowed past.

chapters.title: The Return
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the throne hall amid battle, Silas performs the return: the heir's soul leaves Ada, and her memories of their journey dissolve mid-battle. Silas, drained of his storm-magic, holds the line defenseless. Emotional beat: sacrifice completed at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: What Remains When Memory Burns
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Crowned heir restored, the mountain steadies—but Ada stands among strangers who know her intimately while she knows none of them. She finds Silas's confession letter, written before the return. Emotional beat: grief for a love she cannot remember living.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Unremembering
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The usurper makes a final assault; Ada, guided only by instinct and the letter, fights beside Silas though she doesn't know why she trusts him. Together they break the siege. Emotional beat: loyalty proven deeper than memory.

chapters.title: Begin Again, Storm-Caller
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Peace settled, Silas—powerless, honest, ordinary—asks nothing of Ada. She offers instead to build new memories with him, starting with a charm bought at a market stall. Emotional beat: quiet hope; identity rebuilt not from the past but chosen forward.
